claims.text: The initial Al0.7CoCrFeNi alloy has a dual-phase FCC/B2 lamellar structure with incoherent interfaces.
The initial alloy has high strength but low ductility because stress concentrates at its incoherent phase interfaces.
Treatment at 6 GPa and 1473 K for 2 hours will transform the lamellar topology into a hierarchical microstructure.
The HPHT treatment will transform incoherent FCC/B2 interfaces into coherent or semi-coherent interfaces with reduced misfit.
HPHT drives atomic diffusion and interface restructuring that lowers interfacial energy.
Coherent interfaces can facilitate dislocation transmission across an internal boundary.
The transformed FCC/B2 interfaces will permit dislocation transfer between the FCC and B2 phases with reduced energy barriers.
The transformed microstructure will activate dislocation motion, stacking-fault formation, and twinning.
These deformation mechanisms will operate homogeneously across both FCC and B2 phases.
Coherent interfaces and dislocation transfer will alleviate or eliminate stress concentrations at phase boundaries.
Reducing strain localization at lamellar interfaces will suppress crack initiation or propagation.
The HPHT-treated alloy will achieve uniform elongation greater than 25%.
The HPHT-treated alloy will retain an ultimate tensile strength greater than 1.5 GPa.
The HPHT treatment will overcome the strength-ductility trade-off in Al0.7CoCrFeNi.
Treated fracture surfaces will show elongated cracks or ductile dimples rather than isolated microcracks.
GND densities in the FCC and B2 phases will converge at high tensile strain.
The baseline alloy undergoes brittle fracture with isolated microcracks and strong strain localization in the FCC phase.
Temperatures below 1500 K and pressures below 8 GPa are safe upper bounds for preserving the FCC/B2 eutectic structure.
At 6 GPa and 1473 K, the B2 phase may decompose or the interface transformation may remain incomplete.
The predicted convergence of phase-specific GND densities may depend on strain rate.

contradictions.description: The mechanism claims that interfacial cracking is arrested, but the predicted treated fracture morphology includes elongated cracks. The cited evidence characterizes elongated cracks as products of microcrack propagation and coalescence, making this proposed favorable marker inconsistent with the crack-arrest claim.
